clue.text: Belgrade nun created a bit of folklore

indicators.note: something created is made fresh, so the letters before it are built into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A nun in the Serbian capital gives rise to a piece of local folk tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban legend is a modern myth passed on by word of mouth, a small item of present-day folklore.

clue.text: Transmitted data to the web when excited and sloshed

blocks.note: to be up is to be lively or worked up
loaded is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone posted files online while giddy and drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To upload is to send files from a computer to an internet server, here in the past tense.

clue.text: Organised bride's hen party, ending in perfect gift

indicators.note: organising things puts them into a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged
the ending of a word is its final letter, which is all that is taken

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A well-run hen night for the bride-to-be turns out to be the ideal gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday present is a gift given on someone's birthday, so 'gift' is the general term for it.

clue.text: Snack from snack shop made completely free

indicators.note: each word is freed at both ends, losing its outermost letters so only the inner core is kept

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A café hands out its snacks entirely without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely free' sounds like no charge; it means both words are stripped of their edge letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, eaten as a snack, often with melted cheese.

clue.text: Heads of European Commission touring side of Warsaw that's rather sad

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept
a tour goes all the way around, so the outer letters wrap around the inner piece

blocks.note: the first letter of each word
Legia Warsaw is the Polish capital's best-known football team

explanation.surface: EU commissioners visit the Polish capital in a melancholy mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is a sports team here, not an edge: Legia Warsaw is a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac means mournful, in the manner of an elegy, a poem of lament for the dead.

clue.text: Most difficult to leave Sierra peak

indicators.note: a letter that leaves is no longer there, so it is dropped from the word

blocks.note: superlative of severe
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The hardest Sierra mountain to get down from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sierra' suggests mountains, fitting the peak, but it is just the radio code word for one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the highest mountain in the world, a Himalayan summit on the Nepal–Tibet border.

clue.text: Pursue postgrad Timothy, holding singular fixed opinions

definitions.note: plural phrase for a singular noun; dogmatism is the holding of such opinions

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so the name surrounds the extra letter

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them doggedly
a Master of Arts is a postgraduate degree
short form of the name
standard grammatical abbreviation

explanation.surface: Chase a graduate student called Timothy who has rigid, unshakeable views.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatism is the tendency to assert opinions as certainly true and refuse to reconsider them.

clue.text: Day to get married?

blocks.note: first meaning: the short form of a weekday name
second meaning: to marry, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as asking which day suits a wedding; instead the one word is both an abbreviated weekday and the verb for marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Wed is the standard abbreviation for Wednesday, and also an ordinary verb meaning to marry.

clue.text: Order richest NZ wine to accompany the Spanish escalope

indicators.note: to order things is to put them in a sequence, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A diner asks for New Zealand's fullest wine to go with a Spanish cutlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiener schnitzel is a Viennese dish of thin breaded veal, a classic example of an escalope.

clue.text: Loads turned up to be entertained by party magician

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word upward reads it from bottom to top
a host entertains a guest inside the home, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: loads means a great many
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Crowds arrive to enjoy a conjuror performing at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Dynamo is the stage name of Steven Frayne, a British street magician known from television.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the professional name of a well-known British illusionist, so 'magician' defines him by example.

clue.text: Theatre — opulently rich curtains

indicators.note: curtains hang around and conceal something, so the answer sits inside the words beside it

blocks.note: letters running across the end of one word and into the next

explanation.surface: A playhouse with lavishly luxurious drapes on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' fits a theatre so well it looks like scenery, but it is the verb: the words curtain, or screen, the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyric is a common theatre name, notably the Lyric Theatre on Shaftesbury Avenue in London's West End.

clue.text: Unfading English vicar, laid back, eco-friendly

indicators.note: something laid back is set backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
short for Reverend, a vicar's title
green means environmentally friendly

explanation.surface: A relaxed, environmentally minded English clergyman whose charm never fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' sounds like the vicar's easy-going temperament, but it tells you to reverse his title.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen describes plants that keep their leaves all year, and so anything perennially fresh that does not fade.

clue.text: New hairdo, pet? A vision of beauty!

indicators.note: something new is made over, so the letters are reshaped into another order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A hairdresser compliments a client on her fresh style, calling her a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is the British term of endearment, like 'love', so the line reads as salon chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty, so she embodies a vision of loveliness.

clue.text: The best people for the job had a meal before noon

definitions.text: The best people for the job

blocks.note: past tense of eat
ante meridiem, the morning hours

explanation.surface: The ideal workforce took an early lunch before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-team is an idiom for the most capable group available, the first-choice squad.

clue.text: Flexible time scale sadly can't accommodate Julius

indicators.note: with no room for a guest, those letters are left out of the group
things that go sadly go badly wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
Julius is this puzzle's setter, who refers to himself

explanation.surface: A setter regrets that a schedule has no room for him, despite being adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym in the clue stands for ME, just as 'I' or 'this writer' would.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic describes something that stretches and returns, hence adaptable or flexible.

clue.text: Rubbish excessively periodically hirsute body artist

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods
too means to an excessive degree
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on someone excessively hairy who decorates skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist inks designs into the skin, an artist whose canvas is the human body.

clue.text: Follows stories being narrated

indicators.note: narrating is telling out loud, so the word is identified by its sound

blocks.note: tales are stories

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up with stories as they are being told.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to shadow or follow them closely, as a detective does.

clue.text: Run into Ms Davis, one not preferred by gentlemen?

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: taken as written
Bette Davis, the Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: Bumping into Bette Davis, a woman gentlemen may overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the film title Gentlemen Prefer Blondes; the question mark flags the indirect hint.
explanation.definitionFit: If gentlemen prefer blondes, then a woman with dark hair is the one they supposedly pass over.

clue.text: Approach green area for playing cricket

blocks.note: first meaning: a way of presenting or selling an idea
second meaning: the grass strip between the wickets

explanation.surface: Walking up to a cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' reads as a verb meaning walk towards the ground; it is the noun for a sales line. In cricket the strip between the two sets of stumps has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitch is a persuasive presentation, and also the prepared strip of turf on which cricket is played.

clue.text: What about 1st of August? Call trial

the first of a word is its opening letter, the only one taken

blocks.note: eh is a request to repeat, like 'what?'
the first letter of the month
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A query about a date in early August for summoning a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearing is a session of a court where evidence is heard, in effect a trial.

clue.text: Smelly oil affected hotel owner, stomach pumped out

indicators.note: with its stomach emptied out, the word keeps only its outside letters

blocks.note: camp means exaggerated or theatrical in manner
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the first and last letters only

explanation.definitionFit: Camphor is a strong-smelling waxy substance used in liniments and mothballs, often as an aromatic oil.

clue.text: Red China promoting advanced IT from the south

indicators.note: promoting lifts something to a higher place, so in this down entry the A for advanced moves up one slot
read from the bottom of a down entry, the word comes out backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a Tuscan red wine, so 'Red' defines it in the sense of a glass of red.

clue.text: Perform in theatre, have a drink, throws a tantrum

blocks.note: to act is to perform on stage
to sup is to drink in sips

explanation.surface: An actor's evening: a show, a drink, then a diva's meltdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or show bad temper, as a child does in a tantrum.

clue.text: Conservative embarrassed over beliefs

blocks.note: standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Tory is red-faced about the principles he holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a creed, a set of principles or beliefs that someone holds.

clue.text: No stamina when retired? Swap south for island liveliness

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation, the letter taken out
standard abbreviation, the letter put in

explanation.surface: A pensioner short of energy swaps the south coast for an island and gets some spark back.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means vivacity or spirited energy, the state of being animated and lively.

blocks.note: a gambit is an opening ploy or strategy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf range' reads as a practice ground, but the words split: golf is a letter, range the definition.

clue.text: Staunch hero importing international wine

standard abbreviation
a lion is a brave celebrated person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like an adjective meaning loyal, but it is the verb for stopping blood.

clue.text: Business case for eminent composer

blocks.note: informal short form
the first and last letters only

clue.text: A bit of butter? That comes from a cow
